label: thm-RT
title: THEOREM
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For each $\ell \geq 0$, there is the proper covering map $p_0^{\ell} = p_{\ell} \circ \cdots \circ p_1 \colon M_{\ell} \to M_0$, and the projection map 
  $\widehat{q}_{\ell} \colon \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} \to M_{\ell}$  onto the factor $M_{\ell}$ in \eqref{eq-invlimit}.  
  Let $\widehat{x} \in \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}}$ be a choice of basepoint, and  set $x_{\ell} = \widehat{q}_{\ell}(\widehat{x}) \in M_{\ell}$  and set $\Gamma_0 = \pi_1(M_0, x_0)$. For each $\ell > 0$,  $\Gamma_{\ell}$ is the image of $(p_0^{\ell})_{\#} \colon \pi_1(M_{\ell}, x_{\ell}) \to \Gamma_0$, so ${\mathcal G} = \{\Gamma_{\ell} \mid \ell \geq 0 \}$ is a group chain in $\Gamma_0$.
  
  Let $d_{M_0}$ denote a Riemannian metric on $M_0$ and let $\delta_0 > 0$ be sufficiently small so  that, for all $y \in M_0$, the closed metric ball $B_{M_0}(y, \delta_0) \subset M_0$ of radius $\delta_0$ is convex. In particular, $\delta_0$ is less than the injectivity radius of $M_0$. It follows that for each $y \in M_0$ and $y' \in  B_{M_0}(y, \delta_0)$ there is an isomorphism $\iota_{y',y} \colon \pi_1(M_0, y') \cong \pi_1(M_0, y)$ induced by concatenation with a geodesic path  in $B_{M_0}(y, \delta_0)$  from $y'$ to $y$.
  
  
  
   Finally, since the projection $\widehat{q}_0 \colon \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} \to M_0$  is uniformly continuous, we can choose  ${\varepsilon} >0$   sufficiently small so that  $\widehat{q}_0(B_{\mathfrak{M}}(\widehat{y}, {\varepsilon})) \subset B_{M_0}(y, \delta_0/3)$ for all $\widehat{y} \in \widehat{q}_0^{-1}(y)$, where $B_{\mathfrak{M}}(\widehat{y},{\varepsilon})$ is a ball around $\widehat{y} \in \mathfrak{M}_{\mathcal P}$ with respect to the metric $d_\mathfrak{M}$.
  
   
  Given $h \in {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}}; \widehat{x})$, we first define $\chi(h) \in {\rm Comm}(\Gamma)$. We then   show that $\chi(h)$ is independent of choices, and depends only on the basepoint fixed homotopy class of $h$.
   
Let $h \colon \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} \to \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}}$, then by Theorem~\ref{thm-RT} there exists an increasing  sequence $i_{\ell} \geq \ell$, $\ell \geq 0$,  and maps $\varphi_{i_\ell} \colon M_{i_{\ell}} \to M_\ell$  so that the shuffle diagram \eqref{eq-shuffle} commutes, and for  
 the map  ${\widehat{\varphi}} \colon \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} \to \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}}$ defined by the maps $\{\varphi_{i_{\ell}} \mid \ell \geq 0\}$, we have that $h$ and ${\widehat{\varphi}}$ are ${\varepsilon}$-homotopic.  Let $\widehat{y} = {\widehat{\varphi}}(\widehat{x})$ and set $y_{\ell} = \widehat{q}_{\ell}(\widehat{y}) \in M_{\ell}$.
Then we have the diagram:
  \begin{align} \label{eq-defchi}
 \xymatrix{  \pi_1(  M_{i_0} , x_{i_0}) \ar[d]_{(p_0^{i_0})_{\#}} \ar[r]^{({\varphi}_{i_0})_{\#}} &   \pi_1(M_{0} ,y_0)  \ar[r]_{\cong}^{\iota_{y',y}}  &  \pi_1(M_0 , x_0)   \\
\pi_1(M_0 , x_0) &  &   } 
\end{align}
where $(p_0^{i_0})_{\#} \colon  \pi_1(  M_{i_0} , x_{i_0})  \to \Gamma_{i_0} \subset \Gamma_0$ is an isomorphism onto its image $\Gamma_{i_0}$.
Let $h_{\#} \colon \Gamma_{i_0} \to \Gamma_0$ be  the commensurator defined by the inverse of $(p_0^{i_0})_{\#}$ followed by   $\iota_{y',y} \circ ({\varphi}_{i_0})_{\#}$.  Define  $\chi(h) \in {\rm Comm}(\Gamma_0)$ to be the commensurator class of $h_{\#}$.
 
Next, we show that $\chi(h)$ is independent of the choice of an approximation to $h$ by an induced map. 
Suppose there are given two sequences $\{\varphi_{i_\ell} \colon M_{i_{\ell}} \to M_{\ell} \mid \ell \geq 0\}$ and $\{\psi_{j_\ell} \colon M_{j_{\ell}} \to M_{\ell} \mid \ell \geq 0\}$,   so that the shuffle diagram \eqref{eq-shuffle} commutes for each.
  Moreover,   assume that   the induced maps   ${\widehat{\varphi}} \colon \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} \to \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}}$ and  ${\widehat{\psi}} \colon \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} \to \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}}$   are both ${\varepsilon}$-homotopic to $h$. Thus ${\widehat{\varphi}}$ and ${\widehat{\psi}}$ are $2{\varepsilon}$-homotopic.

    Let $\widehat{y} = {\widehat{\varphi}}(\widehat{x})$ then set  $y_{k} = \widehat{q}_{k}(\widehat{y}) \in M_{k}$ for   $k \geq 0$. Likewise, let
      $\widehat{z} = {\widehat{\psi}}(\widehat{x})$ and set  $z_{k} = \widehat{q}_{k}(\widehat{z}) \in M_{k}$ for   $k \geq 0$.
      Choose an index $k_0 > \max\{i_0, j_0\}$. 
  Then we have two maps:
 \begin{eqnarray*}
\Psi_{{\widehat{\varphi}}} \colon & \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} \stackrel{\widehat{q}_{k_0}}{\longrightarrow} M_{k_0} \stackrel{p^{k_0}_{i_0}}{\longrightarrow} M_{i_{0}} \stackrel{{\varphi}_{i_0}}{\longrightarrow}   M_0\\
\Psi_{{\widehat{\psi}}}  \colon & \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} \stackrel{\widehat{q}_{k_0}}{\longrightarrow} M_{k_0} \stackrel{p^{k_0}_{j_0}}{\longrightarrow} M_{j_{0}} \stackrel{\psi_{j_0}}{\longrightarrow}   M_0   ~ .
\end{eqnarray*}
Now, given $\alpha \in \pi_1(M_{k_0}, x_{k_0})$ choose a  closed curve $\gamma$ in $M_{k_0}$ with basepoint $x_{k_0}$ representing $\alpha$.

Let $\widetilde{\gamma}$ be the lift of $\gamma$ to a curve in   the leaf $L_{\widehat{x}}$ in $\mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}}$ starting at $\widehat{x}$ and which covers $\gamma$. 

 

The images   $\Psi_{{\widehat{\varphi}}}(\widetilde{\gamma})$ and $\Psi_{{\widehat{\psi}}}(\widetilde{\gamma})$ in   $M_0$  of the curve  $\widetilde{\gamma}$ in   $\mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}}$ then lie within $2\delta_0/3$ of each other. By our choice of $\delta_0$,  the  images of the  curves   lie in a convex neighborhood of each other, and hence are homotopic. Thus, they determine the same equivalence class in $\pi_1(M_0, x_0)$. This implies that the definition of $\chi(h)$ on elements of $\Gamma_{k_0}$ agrees using either approximation ${\widehat{\varphi}}$ or ${\widehat{\psi}}$, and $\chi(h)$ does not depend on the choice of an approximating homotopy.

Finally, let $\{h_t \colon \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} \to \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} \mid 0 \leq t \leq 1\} \subset {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}};  \widehat{x})$ be an isotopy. Let ${\varepsilon} > 0$ be as above, then there exists $\lambda > 0$ such that   $| s-t| < \lambda$ implies $d_{\mathfrak{M}}[h_s , h_t] < {\varepsilon}$, where $d_{\mathfrak{M}}[\cdot , \cdot]$ denotes the sup-norm on homeomorphisms induced by $d_{\mathfrak{M}}$.  Then for $n \gg 0$ so that $1/n < \lambda$ we form the sequence of isotopic homeomorphisms $\{h_{i/n} \mid 0 \leq i \leq n\}$ with $d_{\mathfrak{M}}[h_{i/n} , h_{(i+1)/n}] < {\varepsilon}$.
 As above, for each $i$ choose an induced tower map ${\widehat{\varphi}}_i$ which approximates $h_{i/n}$.  Then ${\widehat{\varphi}}_i$ and ${\widehat{\varphi}}_{i+1}$ are $3{\varepsilon}$-homotopic, and so $\chi({\widehat{\varphi}}_i)$ and $\chi({\widehat{\varphi}}_{i+1})$ determine the same class in ${\rm Comm}(\Gamma)$. It follows that 
 $\chi({\widehat{\varphi}}_0)$ and $\chi({\widehat{\varphi}}_n)$ determine the same class in ${\rm Comm}(\Gamma)$.  This shows that $\chi(h)$ depends only on the isotopy class of $h$ hence $\chi$ descends to  a map on ${\rm Mod}(\mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}}, \widehat{x})$. This completes the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm-chi}.
 \endproof

title: REMARK
body_md:
{\rm
 The conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm-chi} can be reformulated in terms of pro-categories.
Theorem~\ref{thm-RT} implies that a homeomorphism $h \colon \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} \to \mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}}$ induces a map $\{ {\varphi}_{i_{\ell}} \}$ in the pro-category of spaces. By the local contractibility of the base $M_0$ the pro-map induces a pro-map in the category of groups, which induces the map $\chi$. This is the approach followed in  \cite{BeringStudenmund2024}.
}

label: lem-topfree
title: LEMMA
body_md:
\label{lem-topfree}
If $\ker ({\mathcal G}) = \{e\}$ then the action $(X_{\mathcal G},\Gamma,\Phi)$ is topologically free.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Note that if $\gamma \cdot x = \gamma' \cdot x$ then $\gamma^{-1} \gamma' \in \Gamma_{\ell}$ for all $\ell > 0$ hence $\gamma^{-1} \gamma'  \in \ker({\mathcal G})$ so $\gamma = \gamma'$. Also note that by continuity of the action ${\rm Fix}(\gamma)$ has empty interior if and only if the closure of ${\rm Fix}(\gamma)$ has empty interior.

Now let $\gamma' \in \Gamma$ such that  that there exists a non-empty open set  $V \subset {\rm Fix}(\gamma')$. Then there exists $\gamma \in \Gamma$ with $\gamma  \cdot x \in V$. Then $\gamma' \cdot \gamma \cdot x = \gamma  \cdot x$, and so $\gamma^{-1} \gamma' \gamma = e$ hence $\gamma' = e$. It follows that each ${\rm Fix}(\gamma)$ has no interior for $\gamma \ne e$, hence $ {\rm Iso}(\Phi)$ is meager.
\endproof

label: def-coherent
title: DEFINITION
body_md:
\label{def-coherent}
   An odometer  $({\mathfrak{X}}, \Gamma, \Phi)$  is \emph{coherent} if for every adapted set $U \subset {\mathfrak{X}}$, the restricted holonomy action map $\Phi_U \colon \Gamma_U \to Homeo(U)$ has finite kernel.
head: environment

label: lem-coherentqa
title: LEMMA
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $({\mathfrak{X}}, \Gamma, \Phi)$ is topologically free, then for every adapted set $U \subset {\mathfrak{X}}$, the restricted holonomy action map $\Phi_U \colon \Gamma_U \to Homeo(U)$ has trivial kernel. Conversely, assume that the action   is  coherent, and let $\gamma \in \Gamma$ be such that there exists a non-empty open set $V \subset {\rm Fix}(\gamma)$. Choose an adapted set $U \subset V$, then $\gamma \in \Gamma_U$ and  $\Phi_U(\gamma) = Id$. By assumption, the kernel of $\Phi_U$ is a torsion subgroup of $\Gamma_U$ hence a torsion subgroup of $\Gamma$. Thus, $\gamma$ is the identity, and so ${\rm Iso}(\Phi)$ is a meager set. 
\endproof

label: ex-product-lqa-coherent
title: EXAMPLE
body_md:
\label{ex-product-lqa-coherent}
{\rm The first example   is that of an action which is effective and coherent, but not topologically free.  It is   a special case of \cite[Example~7.6]{DHL2016a}.

Let $({\mathfrak{X}}_0, \Gamma_0, \Phi_0)$ be a free odometer. For example, this can be a standard odometer action of $\Gamma_0 = {\mathbb Z}$ on the profinite completion $\widehat{{\mathbb Z}}$.
Let $H$ be a non-trivial finite simple group, and $K \subset H$ a proper non-trivial subgroup.
Let $\Gamma = \Gamma_0 \times H$ be the product group, and let ${\mathfrak{X}} =  {\mathfrak{X}}_0 \times H/K$ be the product of ${\mathfrak{X}}_0$ with the finite space $H/K$. Let $\Phi \colon \Gamma \times {\mathfrak{X}} \to {\mathfrak{X}}$ be the product of the   action of   $\Gamma_0$ on the factor ${\mathfrak{X}}_0$, an the left action of  $H$ on the factor $H/K$.

For each $hK \in H/K$, let $U_h = {\mathfrak{X}}_0 \times \{hK\}$ which is an adapted clopen set in ${\mathfrak{X}}$. The subgroup $\Gamma_0$ acts freely on each $U_h$. The subgroup $\{e\} \times K$ fixes every point in the set $U_e = {\mathfrak{X}}_0 \times \{e K \} $, and for any $h \in H$, the conjugate $\{e\} \times hKh^{-1}$ fixes  every point in $U_h$, which implies that the action of $\Gamma$ on ${\mathfrak{X}}$ is not topologically free. The intersection $\bigcap_{h \in H} hKh^{-1}$ is trivial, thus the subgroup $H$ acts effectively on $H/K$ and hence $\Gamma$ acts effectively on ${\mathfrak{X}}$. 
The action of  $\Gamma_{U_h} = \Gamma_0 \times hKh^{-1}$ preserves $U_h$ and the kernel of the action map $\Phi_{U_h} \colon \Gamma_{U_h} \to {\rm Homeo}(U_h)$ is the finite group $\{e\} \times hKh^{-1}$. It follows that this action is effective and coherent.
}

label: prop-nilpotentcoherent
title: PROPOSITION
body_md:
\label{prop-nilpotentcoherent}
 If $\Gamma$   is  nilpotent, then  an  effective odometer       $({\mathfrak{X}}, \Gamma, \Phi)$     is   topologically free.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $U \subset {\mathfrak{X}}$ be an adapted set and let $h\in \Gamma_U$ such that $\Phi_U(h)$ is the identity on $U$. We claim that $\Phi(h)$ acts as the identity on $X_{{\mathcal G}}$.  We proceed by induction on the upper central series
$$\{e\} = \Gamma_{(0)} \subset \Gamma_{(1)} \subset \cdots \subset \Gamma_{(k)} = \Gamma$$
So $\Gamma_{(1)}$ is the center of $\Gamma$, and $\Gamma_{(i+1)} = \{g \in \Gamma \mid [g,h] \in \Gamma_{(i)} \ \forall h \in \Gamma\}$. 
 



Let $g \in \Gamma_{(1)}$, then for $y \in U$, we have 
$h \cdot g \cdot y = g \cdot h \cdot y = g \cdot y$. Thus $\Phi(h)$ acts as the identity on the union of the clopen sets $\{g \cdot U \mid g \in \Gamma_{(1)} \}$.

For $1 \leq i < k$, assume that $\Phi(h)$ acts as the identity on the union of the clopen sets $\{g\cdot U \mid g \in \Gamma_{(i)} \}$.
Let $g \in \Gamma_{(i+1)}$ then for $y \in  U$, we have $[g,h] = g^{-1}h^{-1}g h \in \Gamma_{(i)}$ and
$$h \cdot g \cdot y = h \cdot    g \cdot [g,h]  \cdot y = h \cdot g \cdot g^{-1}h^{-1}g h \cdot y =  g \cdot h \cdot y = g \cdot y.$$ 

 

Thus, $\Phi(h)$ acts as the identity on the union of the clopen sets $\{g\cdot U \mid g \in \Gamma_{(i+1)} \}$.
It follows by finite induction that $\Phi(h)$ acts as the identity on   the union of the clopen sets $\{g \cdot U \mid g \in \Gamma\}$,  which is all of ${\mathfrak{X}}$. Since the action is effective, $h = e$. Thus for every $g \in \Gamma$ the set ${\rm Fix}(g)$ is nowhere dense, and ${\rm Iso}(\Phi)$ is meager.
  \endproof

label: thm-gottalift
title: THEOREM
body_md:
\label{thm-gottalift}
 Let    $(X_{{\mathcal G}}, \Gamma, \Phi)$  be  an effective and coherent   odometer.   Let  $x \in X_{{\mathcal G}}$. Then there exists an injection 
$$\Theta_{{\mathcal G}} \colon {\rm Comm}(X_{{\mathcal G}}, \Gamma, \Phi, x) \to {\rm Comm}(\Gamma)$$
such that  $\chi = \Theta_{{\mathcal G}} \circ \sigma_{{\mathcal P},  \widehat{x}}$. That is, the diagram \eqref{eq-diagram} commutes.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first sketch the idea of the proof.
 For $h \in {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} ; \widehat{x})$, the image $\chi(h) \in {\rm Comm}(\Gamma)$ is defined using the zig-zag maps in \eqref{eq-shuffle} which exist  by the theorems of  Mioduszewski   \cite{Mioduszewski1963} and   Rogers and Tollefson  \cite{RT1972b}. 
More precisely,  
 $\chi(h)$ is defined using a map  ${\varphi}_{i_{\ell}} \colon M_{{i_{\ell}}} \to M_{{\ell}}$ between two  stages of the presentation ${\mathcal P}_{{\mathcal G}}$,  which induces the commensurator map as in \eqref{eq-defchi}.


 The map  $\sigma_{{\mathcal P},  \widehat{x}} \colon {\rm Mod}(\mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} ; \widehat{x}) \to {\rm Comm}(X_{{\mathcal G}}, \Gamma, \Phi, x)$  in  Theorem~\ref{thm-charmap}  is defined   by restricting a given homeomorphism $h \in {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} ; \widehat{x})$ to a transversal neighborhood through $\widehat{x}$, yielding a return equivalence    $h_U \colon U \to V$. Then $h_U$ induces a map $\Theta_U \colon {\mathcal H}_U \to {\mathcal H}_V$ of holonomy groups.

 Thus, the map $\Theta_{{\mathcal G}}$   is obtained by lifting the isomorphism $\Theta_U \colon {\mathcal H}_U \to {\mathcal H}_V$, which is the   holonomy action on a local transversal  to the fibration $\mathfrak{M}_{{\mathcal P}} \to M_0$, to a virtual map   between the fundamental groups of the manifolds in the tower ${\mathcal P}_{{\mathcal G}}$.  
We first prove a technical result.  
 
   \begin{lemma}\label{lem-lifting}
  Let  $(X_{{\mathcal G}}, \Gamma, \Phi)$  be  an effective and coherent odometer, and let $U \subset X_{{\mathcal G}}$ be an adapted set. Then there exists a  finite index subgroup $\Gamma_U' \subset \Gamma_U$   such that the     map  $\Phi_U \colon \Gamma_U' \to {\rm Homeo}(U)$ is   injective.
  \end{lemma}
head: manual

label: lem-lifting
title: LEMMA
body_md:
\label{lem-lifting}
  Let  $(X_{{\mathcal G}}, \Gamma, \Phi)$  be  an effective and coherent odometer, and let $U \subset X_{{\mathcal G}}$ be an adapted set. Then there exists a  finite index subgroup $\Gamma_U' \subset \Gamma_U$   such that the     map  $\Phi_U \colon \Gamma_U' \to {\rm Homeo}(U)$ is   injective.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By assumption, the action is effective, so $\Phi \colon \Gamma \to {\rm Homeo}(X_{{\mathcal G}})$ is injective. Moreover,   the isotropy subgroup  $\Gamma_U \subset \Gamma$ has finite index.
 The kernel $K_U = \ker \{ \Phi_U \colon \Gamma_U \to {\rm Homeo}(U)\} \subset \Gamma$ is a finite group by the coherent hypothesis.
 If the   action is  topologically free, then in fact $K_U$ is trivial and so we can take $\Gamma_U' = \Gamma_U$. 
  
  

  
 
Otherwise, the finite group $K_U$ acts effectively on $X_{{\mathcal G}}$, so for a sufficiently small adapted set $U' \subset U$, every element of  the group $K_U$ acts non-trivially on the set of translates of $U'$. That is,  the   map  $\Phi_U \colon K_U \to {\rm Homeo}(\Gamma_U/\Gamma_{U'})$ is injective.


 Let $C_{U'} = \ker \{ \Phi_{U'} \colon \Gamma \to {\rm Homeo}(\Gamma/\Gamma_{U'}) \}$ be the kernel of the restricted action, which is a normal subgroup with finite index in $\Gamma$. Then   $g \in C_{U'}$ fixes all points in $\Gamma/\Gamma_{U'}$, while $K_U$ acts effectively on $\Gamma/\Gamma_U$, so $g \not\in K_U$. That is, we have  $K_U \cap C_{U'} = \{e\}$, where $e$ is the identity in $\Gamma$.

 
Then $\Gamma'_U =  \Gamma_U \cap C_{U'}$ has finite index in  $\Gamma$, and   the restriction $\Phi_U \colon \Gamma'_U \to {\rm Homeo}(U)$ is injective.
\endproof

label: lem-cG-iso
title: LEMMA
body_md:
\label{lem-cG-iso}
The restriction $\Theta_{{\mathcal G}} \colon {\mathfrak{I}}(X_{{\mathcal G}}, \Gamma, \Phi, x) \to {\rm Aut}_{{\mathcal G}}(\Gamma)$ is an isomorphism.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $h \colon X_{{\mathcal G}} \to X_{{\mathcal G}}$ be an isomorphism such that $h(x) = x$, with   $\Theta = \Theta_{{\mathcal G}}(h) \colon \Gamma \to \Gamma$ the identity. 
The action $\Phi \colon \Gamma \times X_{{\mathcal G}} \to X_{{\mathcal G}}$ is minimal, so the orbit of $x$ is dense in $X_{{\mathcal G}}$.
By the condition \eqref{eq-isomorphism}, we then have
$h \circ \Phi(g) =   \Phi(g) \circ h$ for all $g \in \Gamma$. Apply this to $x$ to obtain $h(\Phi(g) (x)) = \Phi(g)(x)$, 
and so $h$ is the identity on a dense subset of $X_{{\mathcal G}}$, which yields the claim.
\endproof

label: lem-normalizer
title: LEMMA
body_md:
\label{lem-normalizer}
Let $h \in {\mathfrak{I}}(X_{{\mathcal G}}, \Gamma, \Phi)$    be in the kernel of $\Theta_{\mathcal G}$. Let $y = h(x)$ and suppose that $\widehat{g} \in {\mathfrak{G}}_{{\mathcal G}}$  is such that $\overline{\Phi}(\widehat{g})(x) = y$.  Then   $\widehat{g} \in {\mathfrak{N}}_{{\mathcal G}}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We show that  for all $\widehat{k} \in {\mathfrak{D}}_{{\mathcal G}}$, the conjugate   $\widehat{g}^{-1}   \widehat{k}   \widehat{g} \in {\mathfrak{D}}_{{\mathcal G}}$, and thus  $\widehat{g} \in {\mathfrak{N}}_{{\mathcal G}}$.

 
  The map $h$ is an isomorphism of the action, and we assume that $\Theta = \Theta_{\mathcal G}(h)$ is the identity, so by Definition~\ref{def-isomorphism}  we have  $ h \circ \Phi(g) =  \Phi(g) \circ h$ for all $g \in \Gamma$. 

 

Let  $\overline{\Gamma}_{\ell}$ denote the closure of $\Gamma_{\ell}$ in ${\mathfrak{G}}_{{\mathcal G}}$.  Then $\overline{\Gamma}_{\ell}$  acts transitively on $U_{\ell}$, hence $U_{\ell} = \overline{\Gamma}_{\ell}/{\mathfrak{D}}_{{\mathcal G}}$ for all $\ell$. It follows that  $\bigcap_{\ell} \overline{\Gamma}_{\ell} = {\mathfrak{D}}_{{\mathcal G}}$. 
Thus, given  $\overline{k} \in {\mathfrak{D}}_{{\mathcal G}}$,  there exists a sequence $\{k_{\ell} \in \Gamma_{\ell} \mid \ell > 0\}$ such that $\displaystyle \lim_{\ell \to \infty} \overline{k}_{\ell} = \overline{k}$, where $\overline{k}_{\ell}  \in \overline{\Gamma}_{\ell}$ is the image of $k_{\ell}$ in $\overline{\Gamma}_{\ell}$.
 
   
  
 

 We have that $\overline{\Phi}(\overline{k})(x) = x$ and $h(x) = y$, so 
 $\displaystyle \lim_{\ell \to \infty} \Phi(k_{\ell}) (x) = x$ which implies 
    $\displaystyle \lim_{\ell \to \infty}  \Phi(k_{\ell})(y) = y$, so 
$$
  \overline{\Phi}(\widehat{g})(x) = y = \lim_{\ell \to \infty} \Phi(k_{\ell}) ( y) = \lim_{\ell \to \infty}\Phi(k_{\ell}) (\overline{\Phi}(\widehat{g})(x))  = \lim_{\ell \to \infty}\Phi(\overline{k}_{\ell})\overline{\Phi}( \widehat{g})(x) \ ,
$$
and therefore $\displaystyle x =  \lim_{\ell \to \infty}\overline{\Phi}(\widehat{g}^{-1} \overline{k}_{\ell}   \widehat{g})(x) = \overline{\Phi}(\widehat{g}^{-1} \overline{k}   \widehat{g})(x)$. 
Thus $\widehat{g}^{-1} \overline{k}   \widehat{g} \in {\mathfrak{D}}_{{\mathcal G}}$ for all $\overline{k} \in {\mathfrak{D}}_{{\mathcal G}}$,  and so $\widehat{g} \in {\mathfrak{N}}_{{\mathcal G}}$ as was to be shown.
\endproof

label: prop-product
title: PROPOSITION
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $h \in {\mathfrak{I}}(X_{{\mathcal G}}, \Gamma, \Phi)$  which is in the kernel of $\Theta_{{\mathcal G}}$. That is, $h$ is an automorphism of the action. Let $y = h(x)$ then by Lemma~\ref{lem-normalizer} there exists $\widehat{g} \in {\mathfrak{N}}_{{\mathcal G}}$ such that $\overline{\Phi}(\widehat{g})(x) = y$, that is, the coset $y = \widehat{g} \cdot {\mathfrak{D}}_{{\mathcal G}} = {\mathfrak{D}}_{{\mathcal G}} \cdot \widehat{g}$ as $\widehat{g}$ normalizes ${\mathfrak{D}}_{{\mathcal G}}$. 
 Therefore $\rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}^{-1}) \circ h (x) = x$. 
 Then by  Lemma~\ref{lem-cG-iso} the composition $\rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}^{-1}) \circ h$ is the identity, hence $h = \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g})$, so that $h$ is in the image of $\rho_{{\mathcal G}}$ in ${\rm Homeo}(X_{{\mathcal G}})$. 
 \endproof

label: prop-baseleaf
title: PROPOSITION
body_md:
\label{prop-baseleaf}
Assume  that  the baseleaf $L_{\widehat{x}} \subset \mathfrak{M}_{\Phi}$ is simply connected, then the inclusion ${\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; {\widehat{x}}) \subset {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; L_{\widehat{x}})$ induces an   isomorphism ${\rm Mod}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi}; \widehat{x}) \cong  {\rm Mod}_{BLP}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $h \in {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; L_{\widehat{x}})$ and set $\widehat{y} = h(\widehat{x}) \in L_{\widehat{x}}$. Choose an isotopy $\psi_t \in {\rm Homeo}_0(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi})$ with $\psi_0 = id$, and $\psi_1(\widehat{y}) = \widehat{x}$.   Then the composition $\psi_1 \circ h \in {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; \widehat{x})$.  Thus,   ${\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; L_{\widehat{x}})$ is generated by the subgroups ${\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi}; \widehat{x})$ and ${\rm Homeo}_0(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi})$.  It follows that the inclusion composed with  the quotient map, denoted by 
   $\beta \colon {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; \widehat{x}) \to {\rm Mod}_{BLP}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi})$,  is surjective.

Now suppose that $h \in {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi}; \widehat{x})$ is in the kernel of $\beta$, so that $h$ isotopic to the identity map, say by a family $h_t \in {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi})$ with $h_0 = id$ and $h_1 = h$. This defines the map $H \colon \mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} \times [0,1] \to \mathfrak{M}_{\Phi}$ which lifts to a map
\begin{equation}
\widetilde{H} \colon \widetilde{M}_0 \times X_{{\mathcal G}} \times [0,1] \to \widetilde{M}_0 \times X_{{\mathcal G}} \quad , \quad  \widetilde{H}(\widetilde{x}_0, x, 0) =  (\widetilde{x}_0, x) \ . 
\end{equation}
 The homeomorphisms $h_t$ are leaf preserving, so the path  $\alpha(t) = h_t(\widehat{x})$ satisfies $\alpha(0) = \widehat{x}$ and $\alpha(1) = h(\widehat{x}) = \widehat{x}$. As $L_{\widehat{x}}$ is simply connected, the path $\alpha$ is contractible relative the basepoint $\widehat{x}$, and so the holonomy transport of the transversal $X_{{\mathcal G}}$ it determines is trivial. Thus, we can make an equivariant deformation of the lifted map $\widetilde{H}$ so that the path $\widetilde{H}(\widetilde{x}_0, x, t)$ is constant. Then  $h$ is isotopic to the identity map relative the basepoint $\widehat{x}$. It follows that $\beta$ descends to an isomorphism $\overline{\beta} \colon {\rm Mod}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi}; \widehat{x}) \to {\rm Mod}_{BLP}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi})$.
 \endproof

label: prop-nonhomogeneous
title: PROPOSITION
head: environment

label: eq-equivariant
title: Proof
body_md:
For $\gamma \in \Gamma_{{\mathfrak{N}}}$  and  $(\widehat{g}, h) \in    {\mathfrak{A}}_{{\mathcal G}} \times {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; L_{\widehat{x}})$     we have
\begin{eqnarray}\label{eq-equivariant}
\mu_{{\mathcal G}}(\zeta(\gamma)(\widehat{g} , h) )   & = &     \mu_{{\mathcal G}}( \widehat{g} \cdot \overline{\gamma}^{-1} ,  C(\gamma) \circ  h )   \\
& = & \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g} \cdot \overline{\gamma}^{-1})^{-1} \circ  C(\gamma) \circ  h  \nonumber \\
& = &  \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\overline{\gamma} \cdot \widehat{g}^{-1} ) \circ  C(\gamma) \circ  h \nonumber \\
& = &  \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}^{-1} ) \circ \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\overline{\gamma}) \circ  C(\gamma) \circ  h \nonumber  \\
& = &  \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}^{-1} ) \circ   h =  \mu_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}, h)  \  .\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
Thus, the quotient map $\overline{\mu}_{{\mathcal G}}$ is well-defined. It is continuous in the quotient topology. 
 

Next consider the kernel of  $\overline{\mu}_{{\mathcal G}}$.  Recall that ${\mathfrak{D}}_{{\mathcal G}}$ is the kernel of the action   $\rho_{{\mathcal G}} \colon {\mathfrak{N}}_{{\mathcal G}} \to {\rm Homeo}(X_{{\mathcal G}})$, so that $\rho_{{\mathcal G}} \colon  X_{{\mathcal G}} \times {\mathfrak{A}}_{{\mathcal G}} \to X_{{\mathcal G}}$ is an effective action.

  
Suppose that  $h_1, h_2 \in {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; L_{\widehat{x}})$ and $\widehat{g}_1, \widehat{g}_2 \in {\mathfrak{A}}_{{\mathcal G}}$ are such that   
 $\overline{\mu}_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}_1, h_1) = \overline{\mu}_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}_2, h_2)$.
 
Thus 
 $\rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}_1^{-1}) \circ h_1 = \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}_2^{-1}) \circ h_2$.
      Then for $\widehat{g} = \widehat{g}_2^{-1} \   \widehat{g}_1$, we have 
   $$ h_1 \circ h_2^{-1} = \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}_1) \circ   \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}_2^{-1})  = \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}_2^{-1} \   \widehat{g}_1)  = \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}) \ .$$
     Since $h_1 \circ h_2^{-1} \in    {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; L_{\widehat{x}})$, the right action $\rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g})$  must preserve the baseleaf,      
      hence  $ \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g})  = \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\overline{\gamma})$ for some $\gamma \in \Gamma_{{\mathfrak{N}}}$, and thus $\widehat{g} = \overline{\gamma}  \in {\mathfrak{A}}_{{\mathcal G}}$.   
      Thus we have   $h_1 =  \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\overline{\gamma})   \circ h_2$ and so 
\begin{eqnarray}
(\widehat{g}_1, h_1)  = (\widehat{g}_1 , \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\overline{\gamma})   \circ h_2)  & = &  (\widehat{g}_1 , C(\gamma^{-1})   \circ h_2)  \\ 
& \sim_{\zeta}  &  ( \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\overline{\gamma}^{-1})( \widehat{g}_1) , h_2) \nonumber \\
& =  &  ( \widehat{g}_1 \cdot \overline{\gamma}^{-1} , h_2) =  (\widehat{g}_1 \cdot   \widehat{g}_1^{-1}   \widehat{g}_2 , h_2)   =  (\widehat{g}_2 , h_2)  \ .\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
It follows that $\overline{\mu}_{{\mathcal G}}$ is injective, as claimed. 
     \endproof
head: manual

label: thm-normalize
title: THEOREM
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop-nonhomogeneous}, the map 
 $\overline{\mu}_{{\mathcal G}} \colon   {\mathfrak{A}}_{{\mathcal G}} \times_{\zeta} {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; L_{\widehat{x}})    \longrightarrow {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi})$
 is injective. We need to show that the same is true for the induced map on isotopy classes of maps.
 
 
We first extend the map $\overline{\mu}_{{\mathcal G}}$ to an action of ${\mathfrak{A}}_{{\mathcal G}}$ on ${\rm Mod}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; L_{\widehat{x}})$.
That is, me must show that  the action of $\overline{\mu}_{{\mathcal G}}$ preserves the isotopy equivalence classes. 
 Let     $h_t \in {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; L_{\widehat{x}})$, for $0 \leq t \leq 1$, be an isotopy between $h_0$ and $h_1$, then consider a lift to a family of maps 
  \begin{equation}
\widetilde{h}_t \colon ( \widetilde{M}_0 \times X_{{\mathcal G}} ; \widetilde{M}_0 \times \{x\})  \to (\widetilde{M}_0 \times X_{{\mathcal G}}  ; \widetilde{M}_0 \times \{x\})   \quad , \quad 0 \leq t \leq 1  \ . 
\end{equation}

The space $X_{{\mathcal G}}$ is totally disconnected, so for each $\widehat{y} \in \mathfrak{M}_{\Phi}$ the trace curve $t \mapsto h_t(\widehat{y})$, for $0 \leq t \leq 1$, of the isotopy is a leafwise curve. Thus, for $\widehat{g} \in {\mathfrak{A}}_{{\mathcal G}}$ the action of $\rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g})$ on $X_{{\mathcal G}}$ permutes these trace curves, and hence preserves the   isotopy equivalence relation between the maps $h_0$ and $h_1$.
It follows that there is  a well-defined map on the isotopy classes  
\begin{equation}\label{eq-modinduced}
\mu_{{\mathcal G}} \colon  {\mathfrak{A}}_{{\mathcal G}} \times {\rm Mod}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; L_{\widehat{x}})   \to {\rm Mod}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi})  \ .
\end{equation}
For each $\widehat{g} \in {\mathfrak{A}}_{{\mathcal G}}$, the map $\rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g})$ is uniformly continuous on $\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi}$,  and therefore acts uniformly continuous on ${\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi})$. Thus we obtain a continuous action by  $ {\mathfrak{A}}_{{\mathcal G}} $ which descends to an action on the quotient space
\begin{equation}\label{eq-actionmap}
\overline{\mu}_{{\mathcal G}} \colon   {\mathfrak{A}}_{{\mathcal G}} \times_{\zeta}   {\rm Mod}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; L_{\widehat{x}})     \to  {\rm Mod}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi})  \ .
\end{equation}
We next show that the  map \eqref{eq-actionmap}  is injective.  
Let  $h, h' \in {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; L_{\widehat{x}})$ and $\widehat{g}, \widehat{g}' \in {\mathfrak{A}}_{{\mathcal G}}$  be such that   $\rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g})(h)$ and $\rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}')(h')$ are    isotopic. 
Then for $\widehat{g}'' =   \widehat{g}' \cdot \widehat{g}^{-1}$,  the maps $h$ and $\rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}'') \circ h'$ are isotopic in ${\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi})$, and we need to show they are isotopic in ${\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; L_{\widehat{x}})$. 

 

Let    $H \colon \mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} \times [0,1] \to \mathfrak{M}_{\Phi}$ be an isotopy with  
$$h =  H |_{t=0}  \colon \mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} \times \{0\} \to \mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} \quad {\rm  and} \quad  \rho_{{\mathcal G}}(\widehat{g}'') \circ h' =  H |_{t=1}  \colon \mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} \times \{1\} \to \mathfrak{M}_{\Phi}  \  .$$
The map $h$ preserves the leaf $L_{\widehat{x}}$, thus  $h(\widehat{x}) \in L_{\widehat{x}}$ and hence  the trace $H(\widehat{x}, t)$  is a path in $L_{\widehat{x}}$. 

Let $h_t(\widehat{y}) = H(\widehat{y}, t)$ for $\widehat{y} \in \mathfrak{M}_{\Phi}$, which defines $h_t \in {\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi})$.  We have that $h_t(\widehat{x}) = H(\widehat{x}, t) \in L_{\widehat{x}}$ for $0 \leq t \leq 1$, so $h_t$ is an isotopy in ${\rm Homeo}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; L_{\widehat{x}})$. 
 It follows that 
the map $\overline{\mu}_{{\mathcal G}}$ in \eqref{eq-actionmap} is injective.

   
Finally, by   Proposition~\ref{prop-baseleaf} we have  ${\rm Mod}_{BLF}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi}) \cong {\rm Mod}(\mathfrak{M}_{\Phi} ; \widehat{x})$ so that Theorem~\ref{thm-normalize} is proven. 
\endproof
